newsitem.title: UK: Waning US demand hits Brent,other NSea crudes flat.
newsitem.headline: Waning US demand hits Brent,other NSea crudes flat.

text.p: North Sea benchmark Dated Brent weakened on Monday as demand from the U.S. Gulf waned but other grades were notionally steady, underpinned by thin first half February supply, traders said.

Wet Brent fetched Mar Brent +34.5 cents and +26 cents after trading at +48 cents on Friday as fob supply improved amid less enthusiastic interest from U.S. refiners which have already taken millions of barrels of February Brent.
"I was offering at the equivalent of (WTI) minus 70 cents and there was no serious counter," said a trader, who predicted one of the cargoes sold Monday would reappear in Europe.
Brent paper spreads reflected the weaker spot market tone, Feb/Mar slipping a couple of cents to talk around +34 cents and Mar/Apr trading at +39 after deals at +41 on Friday.
CFDs were active, this week's dates trading down from March Brent +31 cents to +29 and Feb 10-14 fetching a weaker March +8.
Traders said the losses were expected and were bringing the market down to more "reasonable" levels.
"The high (Dated) trade on Friday was to a trader who had to cover a short. It was always going to come down with the U.S. unlikely to take much more in the Feb 10-15 period," said one.
March paper was pegged narrowly firmer at $22.37 by 1824 GMT after technical support on IPE futures held at $22.00 a barrel.
Other North Sea grades were quiet as thin supply depressed activity but there was talk of a Feb 15 Ekofisk cargo fetching around Dated +30/+35 cents after trade at +29/+31 on Friday.
In the Mediterranean, the market for sour benchmark Urals was steady, despite expectations of firmer differentials.
A large end-Jan cargo was heard traded on Friday at Dated Brent -75 cents, steady on deals done earlier in the week.
"People are starting to show Feb cargoes and there doesn't seem to be a problem with supply," said one trader.
